calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Tuch’s line (Protas, Dubois and Tuch) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. story.head: Hellebuyck is still perfect at 7-0-0
paras: There were five goals in the first period alone. Pierre-Luc Dubois got the scoring started for the Capitals early in the period, his fourth straight game with a goal. Lenni Hämeenaho made it 1-1 for New Jersey just over three minutes later, and Ryan Leonard put the Capitals back ahead 2-1 later in the period. Connor Brown made it 2-2 for New Jersey on the power play two and a half minutes later. Anthony Beauvillier restored the Caps’ lead a minute and a half later, but Jesper Boqvist made it 3-3 for New Jersey midway through the second. Timo Meier put the Devils up 4-3 on the power play late in the period. The third period was a wild one. Nico Hischier extended the lead to 5-3 shorthanded just 56 seconds into the period. Ilya Protas cut New Jersey’s lead to 5-4 on the power play 26 seconds later, but they got no closer. Evan Rodrigues stretched the lead to 6-4 just under two minutes later, and he scored again into the empty net with a little over three minutes left. The Devils’ Anton Silaev played his first NHL game. Four players had three-point nights: Brown with a goal and two assists, Boqvist with a goal and two assists, Hämeenaho with a goal and two assists, and Luke Hughes with three assists.

The Capitals outshot the Devils 47-33, but the Devils’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Connor Hellebuyck made 43 saves for the Devils, and Charlie Lindgren allowed six goals on 32 shots. Hellebuyck has won all seven of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history. The Devils moved to 15-6-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Capitals dropped to 10-8-0, slipping to fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Jesper Bratt has a point in eight straight games.
